Not published.** Matt Dell · Council · incumbent (held City office 2022–26). Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom and is Joa's to apply or reject. Incumbent rule: Record in the cell; sourced miss caps below Close (max Partial+ 1.5). Alignment compute APPLIED letter for Dell stays **D**. **Pass 2 (2 Sep 2026) — what changed.** Real page `lastmod` dates recovered from the campaign sitemap (the "no lastmod" line was wrong). Four 2026 council actions added that the first pass did not have: the 23 Jul 2026 cooling-bylaw direction, the 23 Jul 2026 derelict-buildings motion, the 24 Nov 2025 infrastructure-reduction motion, the 3 Mar 2026 UDI membership vote and the 7 Apr 2026 curling-club grant. Two cells rise, three dashes become Record, one cell gains a sourced miss. n is unchanged at 14; the mean moves 1.00 → 1.21. **The proposed letter is C under every variation tested.** ## Card

**Evidence flag that touches eight scored cells.** The prose on /policies and its eight theme pages is **2022-vintage text republished on the 2026 site**. Internal evidence: "Earlier this year, an external report about governance in the city showed the public wanted better transparency… **This report shows a new council has work to do**" and "I support many of the recommendations for improved governance from **the 2022 report**." Those sentences were written before the 2022 election. **Ruling applied on this card: it counts as 2026 campaign text.** The 2026 authorized campaign republished it (sitemap `lastmod` 2026-08-04 / 2026-08-24) and the home page links it under the heading **"My priorities for 2026 → View my policies."** Re-publication under a 2026 authorization is adoption. **But it must be put to the candidate before publication**, because eight of the fourteen scored cells rest on this prose (rows 1, 20, 21, 27, 36, 38, 48, 53). If Dell says the policies pages are legacy content not his 2026 programme, those eight cells drop to 📋 Record and n falls to 6. ### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **record** Named YES on the 7 May 2026 budget (7.28 overall / 9.34 residential). "They want to protect the things that we love in the city." No cap, formula or glide path. **Against interest, added pass 2:** on 24 Nov 2025 he moved to reduce the infrastructure allocation from 5.5M to 4M dollars to help hold the rate, carried 7–2 — a restraint action, but on capital renewal, not a rule on the residential rate. [Times Colonist budget](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094) · [Victoria Buzz 2026 financial plan](https://victoriabuzz.com/2025/11/victoria-saves-more-services-from-cuts-in-2026-financial-plan/) vote 7 May 2026 / press 9 May 2026 · motion 24 Nov 2025

Thompson the derelict-and-neglected-buildings motion carried unanimously 23 Jul 2026 — "This is especially important in the downtown core, where we've seen some prominent buildings sit empty for many years." That is a property-condition instrument, not a public-order one. [record page](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) · [Victoria Buzz 24 Jul 2026](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/07/victoria-passes-motions-on-derelict-buildings-and-air-conditioners-in-rental-units/) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02 · motion 23 Jul 2026

No unit target and no 25/20/15/30 composition mix. Record: named YES on Missing Middle, 26 Jan 2023. [/housing](https://www.mattdell.ca/housing) lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear on any 2026 page. — —

Directional, not costed: no tax formula, no permit benchmark, no dashboard, no 25M-dollar threshold. /endorsements says only "More coming soon…" and /yourvision is a contact form, not a platform. --- ## The 12 topics No topic gets its own letter. Area columns stay blank. Rules as written on . Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date**. A dash is unknown, not a fail. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Partial 1.0** "We need to get back on track and speed up new rental, affordable, social and market housing. I commit to making that happen as soon as possible." · Commits to a supply mix with **no unit target and no composition share**. M6 asks for 12,000+ net new homes and stacked shares of 25% missing middle / 20% three-bedroom / 15% non-market / 30% purpose-built rental; none of the four appears. Record, matching, not a second mark: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023; Family Housing Policy (3-bedroom incentive) on the Record page. **Added pass 2, Record context:** his 6 Dec 2025 open letter to View Royal — "Build housing, stop complaining!" — states Victoria "has approved over 7,000 housing units this term and is ahead of provincial targets." That is a volume claim from before his 31 Dec 2025 declaration, so it is Record, not a 2026 campaign sentence, and it still carries no composition share. The 9,000-units figure is campaign-attributed and is not stamped. [/housing](https://www.mattdell.ca/housing) · [Times Colonist Missing Middle](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676) · [Island Social Trends 7 Dec 2025](https://islandsocialtrends.ca/build-housing-stop-complaining-says-victoria-councillor-dell-to-view-royal/) plan lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 26 Jan 2023 · letter 6 Dec 2025
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — Non-market / rental acceleration is scored on row 1. No City land bank, acquisition fund or co-op financing. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening — No permit-time standard by category and nothing on AI pre-screening. Missing Middle's staff-level permits sit inside the vote already scored on row 1. His 2023 Citified answer — "Councils need to delegate more decision making to staff" — is 2023 words, not a 2026 campaign sentence, and carries no published benchmark either way. — —
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved standard designs do not appear. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Reduced development cost charges for affordable housing by 100%." No named Dell yes/no opened this pass. No 2026 vacancy target and no suite amnesty. Shown, not scored. Do not invent a roll-call. [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — No unified command, co-location or downtown operations desk. CSWB and OUR DWTN are not a Public Order Team. Launch line "keep investing in community safety and wellbeing" is a Mention of safety with no POT instrument, so a dash in every column. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response — No civilian dispatched-response team position. Harm-reduction language on the Record page is health-side, not a crisis-response instrument. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement hours and no staffing number. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — No position on targeting chronic disorder drivers with data. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws — No 2026 bylaw-enforcement sentence. FLAG: Times Colonist 19 Jul 2024 names Kim as "the lone vote against" stepped-up daytime sheltering, 8–1. Dell is not named. Do not invent a roll-call. — —
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — Buffer zones and child-focused spaces do not appear. Harm reduction on the Record page is not a buffer bylaw. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Ended sheltering in Topaz, Stadacona, Vic West, Irving, Central, Hollywood and Beacon Hill park by hiring a Housing Relocation Coordinator to work with people to find suitable homes." No 2026 continue-sentence, no named Dell yes/no opened this pass, no night lighting. Shown, not scored. **Note pass 2:** the 23 Jul 2026 derelict-buildings motion is scored on row 18, not here — derelict private buildings are not M36 public spaces. [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Opposed −1.0** "Voting for the budget were councillors Matt Dell, Jeremy Caradonna, Chris Coleman, Dave Thompson, Krista Loughton and Mayor Marianne Alto." Adopted 7.28 overall / 9.34 residential. Disagrees with a capped residential glide path. Context, same debate, not a second mark: "They want to protect the things that we love in the city." / "If you want to cut the budget, put forward programs people love." **Added pass 2, against interest:** on 24 Nov 2025 Dell moved to cut the infrastructure allocation from 5.5M to 4M dollars, with add-back if non-market-change tax revenue exceeded 1M, carried 7–2 — he did move a restraint measure, but on capital renewal rather than a rule on the residential rate, and the residential rate still landed at 9.34%. That motion is scored as Record on row 30 and as the sourced miss on row 28. The 2023–25 "lowest municipal tax increase of most surrounding major cities" line is a comparative frame, not a restraint instrument, and is not scored. [Times Colonist budget](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094) · [Victoria Buzz 24 Nov 2025](https://victoriabuzz.com/2025/11/victoria-saves-more-services-from-cuts-in-2026-financial-plan/) vote 7 May 2026 / press 9 May 2026 · motion 24 Nov 2025 / press 24 Nov 2025
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — No over-collection refund, no debt rule, no supermajority override. The budget vote is scored on row 13. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. "Tackling affordability" on the home page is housing and business, scored on rows 1 and 18. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger — No published downloading ledger and no refusal threshold. Province-blaming as a frame is not a source. His 6 Dec 2025 View Royal letter argues the opposite direction — that the Province alone can remedy inter-municipal displacement — which is a jurisdiction argument, not a downloading ledger, and is not scored. — —
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — Regional water rates and the filtration plant do not appear. CREST / Harbour Authority seats are seats held, not a source. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Close 2.0** **"Victorians work hard to make this a great place to live, so it's not acceptable for property owners to let their buildings remain empty or fall into disrepair… This is especially important in the downtown core, where we've seen some prominent buildings sit empty for many years."** · Commits: he moved the motion with Coun. Thompson and it **carried unanimously 23 Jul 2026**, directing staff to report back on strengthening bylaws and enforcement tools for derelict and neglected properties, to scan comparable municipalities, and to assess **whether provincial legislative change is needed**. **Comparable instrument** to M71's existing levers (vacant property licensing, conditions on business-licence renewal) and to M71's advocacy for provincial enabling legislation to surcharge persistent commercial vacancies. **Not Aligned:** no 11%-to-5% vacancy target, no quarterly vacancy report by block and sector, no employment-lands no-net-loss rule, and the motion is a report-back rather than the lever itself. Context, not a second mark: home-page "More supports for local business and tourism"; Record-page downtown tax-reduction, facade and Douglas Street funds. OUR DWTN cleanliness is row 26. No sourced miss on this cluster, so Close is allowed. [Victoria Buzz 24 Jul 2026](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/07/victoria-passes-motions-on-derelict-buildings-and-air-conditioners-in-rental-units/) · [Victoria News 20 Jul 2026](https://vicnews.com/2026/07/20/victoria-aims-to-deal-with-derelict-neglected-or-vacant-investment-sites/) · [home](https://www.mattdell.ca/) motion 23 Jul 2026 / press 20 and 24 Jul 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No 15-minute grace, no capital-approval threshold, no permit-fee schedule. First-hour free is a Year-2 gated item, not a Year-1 instrument. Crystal Pool is scored on row 39, not as a threshold rule. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. **Partial 1.0** "I support the City's commitment to Reconciliation with the Esquimalt and Songhees Nation, and will work collaboratively with local First Nations to implement the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Calls to Action." · Commits to a City TRC-implementation action. **Neither:** no standing government-to-government table (M1), no Indigenous procurement standard (M2), no place-names-and-signage programme (M3), no cultural protocols (M4), no urban Indigenous services liaison (M5). The footer lək̓ʷəŋən acknowledgement is not a second mark. Record-page PEERS Indigenous-led return programme is not this Foundation package and is not scored here. [/reconciliation](https://www.mattdell.ca/reconciliation) lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Aligned 3.0** **Commits, same instrument, on the M64 indoor-heat limb.** Dell moved the motion with Couns. Thompson and Caradonna in May 2026; the resulting staff direction was **approved unanimously 23 Jul 2026** and directs staff to report back on **amendments to the City's Rental Property Standards of Maintenance Bylaw ensuring no prohibition of cooling devices in rental units**, including passive cooling. The Program names that instrument in the same words: M64's first ordered step is to "ban unreasonable landlord prohibition of portable cooling, **if the Standards of Maintenance Bylaw** or the business-licence power can carry it." Same bylaw, same prohibition-on-the-prohibition, and the Program's 26°C performance rule is itself gated to a solicitor's hook — so a legal-feasibility direction is the Program's own step at this stage, not a substitute for it. 2026 campaign sentence, context, not a second mark: "we must accelerate construction of non-market housing, build thousands of new rental units, and strengthen policies to protect renters." Record, matching: Tenant Protection Bylaw; 30 Jul 2026 council unanimously enhanced displacement compensation. **FLAG 1 — cluster:** M9b short-term-rental licensing is entirely absent and M9's demoviction package is Record rather than a 2026 promise; a reader who scores the cluster rather than the instrument holds this at Close 2.0. **FLAG 2 — accuracy, and it is the cap question:** in his 30 Jul 2026 Facebook post Dell wrote that council gave renters "the strongest protections in the Province" and that "the City also hired a Tenant Protection Coordinator." The vote was unanimous, the largest enhancement was Hammond's amendment, and the City's own Tenant Relocation Guide has the coordinator **appointed and paid by the applicant**. That is an overstatement of his own role, not a vote contradicting a promise, so the incumbent cap is **not** applied here. If Joa rules it a sourced miss, this cell caps at Partial+ 1.5. [Victoria Buzz 24 Jul 2026](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/07/victoria-passes-motions-on-derelict-buildings-and-air-conditioners-in-rental-units/) · [CHEK, council votes to explore cooling requirements](https://cheknews.ca/victoria-council-votes-in-favour-of-exploring-new-cooling-requirements-for-rental-apartments-1324502/) · [Victoria News 14 May 2026](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/14/cool-heads-prevail-victoria-unanimously-seeks-info-on-keeping-renters-cool/) · [/housing](https://www.mattdell.ca/housing) · [Times Colonist tenant compensation](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/compensation-hiked-for-long-term-victoria-tenants-displaced-by-development-12613134) motion May 2026, adopted 23 Jul 2026 / press 14 May and 24 Jul 2026 · plan lastmod 2026-08-04 · compensation vote 30 Jul 2026
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — No published algorithmic waitlist and no by-name / HIFIS sentence in Dell's own name this pass. Another councillor's HIFIS file is not a Dell sentence. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Approved 517 units of shelter and supportive housing for individuals experiencing homelessness." No Housing First target, no STEP throughput, no quarterly count, no 2026 Dell-owned Housing First sentence. Shown, not scored. [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02

# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date

Parent / Little League / PAC background is not a source. Record-page free youth bus passes (13–17) is a transit item inside row 27's cluster, not an M13c programme, and is not scored here. — —

### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Started the OUR DWTN program, which invests nearly 900,000 dollars annually into downtown cleanliness, safety and cultural events." His 2023 Citified answer gives the founding figure as a "new 980,000-dollar annual Downtown Revitalization Program." No 2026 continue-sentence, no 90% graffiti-in-48-hours standard, no sanitation hours, no pest plan. Shown, not scored. Arts and events in the same bullet are not a second M50 mark. [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) · [Citified Q&A 10 Aug 2023](https://victoria.citified.ca/news/qa-victoria-councillor-matt-dell-housing-missing-middle-clean-streets-future/) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02 · Q&A 10 Aug 2023
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) **Partial 1.0** "Expand clean and active transportation options and public transit - so everyone can get around Victoria easily and at reasonable cost." · Commits to active transportation. **Neither:** no adaptive-signal programme (M19), no collision-ranked intersection inventory (M38), no school-zone automated speed enforcement (M40), no named corridor. Transit in the same sentence is not a second M20b/M23b mark. Record AAA cycling, bike share and bike valet are matching context, not a second mark. M39 is struck and is not scored. A 2023 speed-camera motion he seconded is Record context on this cluster, not a 2026 instrument. [/climatechange](https://www.mattdell.ca/climatechange) lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls **Partial 1.0** · incumbent cap engaged "Invest in streets, sidewalks & infrastructure." · Commits to sidewalk and street investment. **Neither:** no sidewalk-gap inventory, no km-of-gap-closed figure, no crossing standard, no City-controlled transit-lever list. **Sourced miss, added pass 2 — actions over words.** On 24 Nov 2025 Dell moved to reduce the City's infrastructure allocation **from 5.5M to 4M dollars**, carried **7–2**; Victoria Buzz reports the reduction could affect "roadwork, the city's fleet, parks' infrastructure, and playgrounds." M20b states that sidewalk and crossing construction is "a named allocation inside M25… not new capital" — that is, inside the very envelope he moved to cut. The 2026 promise sits under the action as context. Cap applied: this cell **cannot exceed Partial+ 1.5**; it scores Partial 1.0 on its own terms, so the cap does not bite. **FLAG:** a reader could hold the action to be a Disagrees and mark Weak 0.5 or Opposed −1.0; the add-back condition (restore if non-market-change revenue exceeded 1M dollars) and the budget-balancing context are why this pass does not. [home](https://www.mattdell.ca/) · [Victoria Buzz 24 Nov 2025](https://victoriabuzz.com/2025/11/victoria-saves-more-services-from-cuts-in-2026-financial-plan/) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · motion 24 Nov 2025 / press 24 Nov 2025
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Committed 14 million dollars to rebuild every public washroom in Victoria." No 2026 washroom-count or universal-accessibility-audit sentence, no named Dell yes/no opened this pass. Shown, not scored. [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02
30 M25 fix roads first 📋 Record **Added pass 2.** "Councillor Matt Dell put forth a motion to reduce the City's infrastructure funding from 5.5 million to 4 million dollars," with add-back "if any Non-Market Change (NMC) tax revenue comes in, in excess of 1 million, that it be added back into the infrastructure budget." Carried **7–2**, 24 Nov 2025, during deliberations that were trying to bring the 2026 increase down toward 4%. M25 is a zero-net-new sequencing rule inside the existing envelope (11.5M major plus 3.5M local street rehabilitation in 2026), so a reduction of the envelope is a decision **about** M25's money without being a vote against M25's sequencing rule. Recorded here, scored as the sourced miss on row 28. No pothole report-to-fix standard and no published quarterly road-condition ranking. **Adjacency rule applied: Record, not Opposed.** [Victoria Buzz 24 Nov 2025](https://victoriabuzz.com/2025/11/victoria-saves-more-services-from-cuts-in-2026-financial-plan/) motion 24 Nov 2025 / press 24 Nov 2025, retrieved 2026-09-02

# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date

No named Dell yes/no opened this pass, and no exposure-based cost-spreading design. The downtown-business 2026 material is scored on row 18. Shown, not scored. ### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues **Close 2.0** "To do this, we must implement strategies in cooperation with the arts community, preserve important venues and provide grant funding for diverse artists to create work for the public." · Commits to cultural-venue preservation (M46b). **Comparable, not Same:** strict heritage design standards (M43) and the street-furniture restoration programme (M44) are not named. The grant-funding clause in the same sentence is not a second M50b mark. Record, matching, not a second mark: acquired Hermann's Jazz Club and built the Ship Point outdoor venue. Royal and McPherson board seat is a seat held, not a source. No sourced miss on this cluster, so Close is allowed. FLAG: a reader could argue Partial 1.0 because heritage standards are absent; ambiguity resolves upward. [/artsculture](https://www.mattdell.ca/artsculture) · [Victoria News launch 31 Dec 2025](https://vicnews.com/2025/12/31/victoria-coun-matt-dell-launches-his-bid-for-re-election-to-council/) plan lastmod 2026-08-04, retrieved 2026-09-02 · launch 31 Dec 2025
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Supported pedestrianized areas across the city, including lower Government Street and other neighbourhood led spaces." No 2026 pedestrianisation-pilot sentence and no resident-chosen, referendum-approved signature project. "Walkable neighbourhoods" on the home page is branding, not pedestrianisation. His 2023 Citified answer names Centennial Square revitalisation as a goal, which is 2023 words and not a 2026 instrument. Shown, not scored. [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) lastmod 2026-08-13, retrieved 2026-09-02
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks **Partial 1.0** "We need to preserve green space and invest in new parks with inclusive amenities, and we must invest in recreation facilities for everyone – such as a new Crystal Pool and Central Library." · Commits to new parks investment (M49). **Neither:** no heritage-incentive schedule (M47), no extended ornamental-lighting hours (M48), no waterfront-walkway expansion. Crystal Pool in this sentence is context; the dated 2030 completion is scored on row 39. FLAG: home-page "Climate-smart city with more parks & trees" is a different sentence, scored on row 49.
